timeline_disposition.reason: Mipham (1846–1912), also known as Mipam Gyatso and Ju Mipham, is a securely historical Tibetan Buddhist philosopher and one of the most influential modern systematizers of Nyingma philosophy. His documented intellectual career spans the Derge/Kham region, several monasteries and teachers, and cross-school study within the Rime milieu. The reviewed evidence therefore does not justify reducing his philosophical activity to one exact canonical polity interval. ATLAS retains the historical Person without manufacturing a single polity-bound Activity rail.

sources.title: Mipam — Oxford Research Encyclopedia of Religion
sources.citation_text: Oxford identifies Mipam or Mipham (1846–1912) as one of the most influential figures in the Tibetan Buddhist world in the last five hundred years and highlights his systematic contributions to Nyingma philosophy, Madhyamaka, epistemology, and Dzogchen.

sources.title: Mipam Gyatso — The Treasury of Lives
sources.citation_text: The peer-reviewed Treasury of Lives records Mipam Gyatso, 1846–1912, as a historical Tibetan master born in Derge and associated with multiple Nyingma, Kagyu, Geluk, and Sakya teachers and institutions.
